_comment: When enough of a street has been seen for it to count as walked. Three consumers must agree on these numbers,
which is why they live here rather than in any one of them: Explore credits a street from the stretches its
panos covered (Task.recordVisit, StreetProgress), the server decides audit_task.completed from the same
stretches (models.audit.StreetCoverage), and tools/city/check_streets_for_imagery.py decides whether a street
has imagery at all. If they disagreed, the scan would keep a street open that Explore can never finish, and
labelers would be sent down it again and again (#5669, #5091).
Fitted to the pano trails of 115k regular audits fleet-wide (#5733): an end-to-end walk leaves up to 30 m
unseen at its ends, so a 90% floor fails 40% of real walks, and under 100 m the cap alone would let one pano
at a corner earn the street.
maxUncoveredM: most of a street that may stay unseen; the limit that matters above 100 m.
minCoveredFrac: least share of a street that must have been seen; the limit that matters under 100 m.
panoWindowM: how far either side of a pano counts as seen, roughly GSV's pano spacing.
maxHopM: longest step between consecutive on-street panos whose in-between stretch counts as walked.
